title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
author_bio: James Clear writes and speaks about habits, decision-making, and continuous improvement.
description: A practical framework for building good habits, breaking bad ones, and making small changes that compound over time.

title: The Psychology of Money
author: Morgan Housel
author_bio: Morgan Housel is a financial writer known for explaining money and investing through human behavior.
description: Short stories explore how luck, risk, behavior, and personal experience shape the way people think about money.

title: Deep Work
author: Cal Newport
author_bio: Cal Newport is a computer science professor and author who writes about work, technology, and focus.
description: A guide to cultivating distraction-free concentration for demanding work in an increasingly connected world.

title: Digital Minimalism
author: Cal Newport
author_bio: Cal Newport is a computer science professor and author who writes about work, technology, and focus.
description: A philosophy for using technology more intentionally and making room for activities that matter most.

title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
author: Stephen R. Covey
author_bio: Stephen R. Covey was an educator and author known for his work on leadership and personal effectiveness.
description: A principles-based approach to personal and professional effectiveness, from taking initiative to working collaboratively.

title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
author: Dale Carnegie
author_bio: Dale Carnegie was a writer and instructor whose work focused on communication and interpersonal skills.
description: Classic guidance on communicating well, building relationships, and handling everyday interactions constructively.

title: Mindset
author: Carol S. Dweck
author_bio: Carol S. Dweck is a psychologist known for research on motivation and mindsets.
description: Explains how beliefs about ability can influence learning, resilience, achievement, and responses to setbacks.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
author_bio: Daniel Kahneman was a psychologist and Nobel laureate whose work transformed the study of judgment and decision-making.
description: An overview of two modes of thought and how mental shortcuts can shape judgment and decision-making.

title: Grit
author: Angela Duckworth
author_bio: Angela Duckworth is a psychologist whose research focuses on grit, achievement, and character.
description: Examines the roles of passion and perseverance in pursuing long-term goals.

title: Essentialism
author: Greg McKeown
author_bio: Greg McKeown writes and teaches about essentialism, leadership, and disciplined prioritization.
description: A method for identifying what matters most and making deliberate trade-offs instead of trying to do everything.

title: Make Time
author: Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky
author_bio: Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky are designers and authors who write about attention, habits, and time.
description: A collection of practical tactics for protecting daily priorities from distraction and designing more intentional days.

title: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
author: Mark Manson
author_bio: Mark Manson is an author known for direct, conversational writing on values and personal development.
description: A blunt, irreverent look at choosing worthwhile values and accepting the limits and difficulties of life.

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
author_bio: Eckhart Tolle is a spiritual teacher and author whose work focuses on presence and awareness.
description: Introduces practices for paying attention to the present moment and examining habitual thought patterns.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
author_bio: Viktor E. Frankl was a psychiatrist and neurologist who founded logotherapy, an approach centered on meaning.
description: Combines Frankl's account of survival in Nazi concentration camps with reflections on meaning and purpose.

title: Ikigai
author: Héctor García and Francesc Miralles
author_bio: Héctor García and Francesc Miralles are authors who write about Japanese culture, well-being, and purpose.
description: Explores the Japanese concept of ikigai and shares perspectives on purpose, community, and daily routines.

title: Start with Why
author: Simon Sinek
author_bio: Simon Sinek is an author and speaker whose work focuses on leadership, purpose, and organizations.
description: Argues that communicating a clear purpose can help leaders and organizations inspire people and build trust.

title: The Lean Startup
author: Eric Ries
author_bio: Eric Ries is an entrepreneur and author known for developing the Lean Startup methodology.
description: Presents a method for testing business ideas through rapid experimentation, validated learning, and iterative product development.

title: Zero to One
author: Peter Thiel and Blake Masters
author_bio: Peter Thiel is an entrepreneur and investor; Blake Masters is an entrepreneur and writer.
description: Explores entrepreneurship, innovation, and the challenge of creating businesses that offer something genuinely new.

title: Rich Dad Poor Dad
author: Robert T. Kiyosaki
author_bio: Robert T. Kiyosaki is an author and entrepreneur known for writing about financial education.
description: Uses contrasting financial perspectives to discuss assets, liabilities, financial literacy, and independent thinking about money.

title: Sapiens
author: Yuval Noah Harari
author_bio: Yuval Noah Harari is a historian and author whose work examines human history and long-term social change.
description: A broad history of humankind, from early human societies to the institutions and technologies of the modern world.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
author_bio: Stephen Hawking was a theoretical physicist whose research and books helped communicate cosmology to broad audiences.
description: An accessible introduction to cosmology, covering space, time, black holes, and major questions about the universe.

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
author_bio: Carl Sagan was an astronomer and science communicator known for making scientific ideas accessible to the public.
description: A wide-ranging journey through astronomy, scientific discovery, and humanity's place in the universe.

title: The Gene: An Intimate History
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
author_bio: Siddhartha Mukherjee is a physician, researcher, and author of books on biology and medicine.
description: Traces the history of genetics while exploring how genes influence medicine, identity, and our understanding of heredity.

title: The Body Keeps the Score
author: Bessel van der Kolk
author_bio: Bessel van der Kolk is a psychiatrist and researcher known for work on trauma and its treatment.
description: Discusses trauma and its effects on the brain and body, along with therapeutic approaches to recovery.

title: The Hidden Life of Trees
author: Peter Wohlleben
author_bio: Peter Wohlleben is a forester and author who writes about forest ecology and tree behavior.
description: Presents forests as interconnected living communities and describes scientific findings about tree growth and communication.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
author_bio: Paulo Coelho is a Brazilian novelist whose fiction often explores spirituality and personal journeys.
description: A young shepherd travels in search of treasure and encounters lessons about dreams, courage, and listening to one's heart.

title: The Midnight Library
author: Matt Haig
author_bio: Matt Haig is a British novelist and non-fiction author whose work often explores mental health and hope.
description: A woman finds a library where each book offers a chance to explore a different version of her life.

title: The Book Thief
author: Markus Zusak
author_bio: Markus Zusak is an Australian novelist known for character-driven fiction for young adults and adults.
description: Narrated by Death, this novel follows a young girl who discovers the power of words in Nazi Germany.

title: Where the Crawdads Sing
author: Delia Owens
author_bio: Delia Owens is an author and wildlife scientist whose writing includes nature and fiction.
description: A young woman raised in the marshes of North Carolina becomes connected to a local investigation after a death.

title: A Man Called Ove
author: Fredrik Backman
author_bio: Fredrik Backman is a Swedish novelist known for warm, character-focused stories.
description: A grumpy, routine-loving neighbor finds his life changing when a lively family moves in next door.

title: The Kite Runner
author: Khaled Hosseini
author_bio: Khaled Hosseini is an Afghan-American novelist whose work often explores family, migration, and Afghanistan.
description: A story of friendship, betrayal, and atonement set against decades of change in Afghanistan.

title: Normal People
author: Sally Rooney
author_bio: Sally Rooney is an Irish novelist known for contemporary fiction about relationships and class.
description: Follows two young people from the same Irish town as their relationship evolves through school and university.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
author_bio: Alex Michaelides is a novelist known for psychological thriller fiction.
description: A psychotherapist works with a famous painter who has stopped speaking after a violent incident involving her husband.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
author_bio: Andy Weir is a novelist known for science-driven speculative fiction.
description: A lone astronaut wakes with no memory of his mission and must solve a scientific mystery to help save humanity.

title: The Thursday Murder Club
author: Richard Osman
author_bio: Richard Osman is a British author, television presenter, and producer.
description: Four residents of a retirement community investigate a local murder and discover that their hobby is more than a game.

title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
author: J. K. Rowling
author_bio: J. K. Rowling is a British author best known for the Harry Potter fantasy series.
description: Harry discovers he is a wizard and begins his education at Hogwarts, where he uncovers secrets about his past.

title: The Hobbit
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
author_bio: J. R. R. Tolkien was a scholar and writer whose works helped shape modern fantasy literature.
description: Bilbo Baggins leaves his comfortable home to join a company of dwarves on a quest involving a dragon and a lost treasure.

title: The Fellowship of the Ring
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
author_bio: J. R. R. Tolkien was a scholar and writer whose works helped shape modern fantasy literature.
description: Frodo and a diverse fellowship begin a perilous journey to destroy a powerful ring that threatens Middle-earth.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
author_bio: Frank Herbert was an American science-fiction author best known for the Dune saga.
description: On the desert planet Arrakis, political intrigue and control of a valuable resource shape the fate of a young heir.

author: George Orwell
author_bio: George Orwell was an English novelist and essayist whose work examined politics, power, and language.
description: In a totalitarian society under constant surveillance, Winston Smith struggles to preserve independent thought and truth.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
author_bio: Harper Lee was an American novelist best known for this classic novel about justice and empathy.
description: Through a child's perspective, a Southern community confronts racial injustice, empathy, and moral courage.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
author_bio: Jane Austen was an English novelist whose work examines manners, family, class, and relationships.
description: Elizabeth Bennet and Fitzwilliam Darcy navigate first impressions, family expectations, and changing feelings in Regency England.

title: Fahrenheit 451
author: Ray Bradbury
author_bio: Ray Bradbury was an American author known for imaginative fiction about society, technology, and human nature.
description: In a society that bans books, fireman Guy Montag begins to question censorship and the cost of conformity.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
author_bio: Andy Weir is a novelist known for science-driven speculative fiction.
description: Stranded on Mars, astronaut Mark Watney uses engineering, science, and resourcefulness to try to survive until rescue.

title: The Hunger Games
author: Suzanne Collins
author_bio: Suzanne Collins is an American author known for the Hunger Games series and children's fiction.
description: Katniss Everdeen volunteers for a televised fight to the death and becomes a symbol of resistance in a divided nation.

title: The Fault in Our Stars
author: John Green
author_bio: John Green is an American novelist and video creator known for young-adult fiction.
description: Two teenagers who meet at a cancer support group develop a relationship while grappling with illness, love, and meaning.

title: The Design of Everyday Things
author: Don Norman
author_bio: Don Norman is a researcher and author known for human-centered design and usability.
description: Explains how thoughtful design can make everyday objects easier to understand, use, and operate safely.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
author_bio: Robert C. Martin is a software engineer and author known for work on agile development and software design.
description: Offers principles and examples for writing readable, maintainable code and improving software craftsmanship.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: David Thomas and Andrew Hunt
author_bio: David Thomas and Andrew Hunt are software developers and authors focused on practical engineering principles.
description: Practical advice for improving software development habits, technical judgment, debugging, and long-term engineering skills.

title: Thinking in Systems
author: Donella H. Meadows
author_bio: Donella H. Meadows was an environmental scientist and systems analyst known for work on complex systems.
description: Introduces systems thinking through feedback loops, stocks, flows, and ways to understand complex interconnected problems.
